stories.headline: Cerebras Prices IPO at $185, Above Range, Raising $5.55B at $56.4B Valuation

key_facts.fact: Cerebras Systems priced its IPO at $185 per share on May 13, above the marketed range of $150-$160, selling 30 million Class A shares to raise $5.55 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras Systems Inc. today announced the pricing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 30,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock, at a public offering price of $185.00 per share.

key_facts.fact: At the IPO price, Cerebras is valued at $56.43 billion on a fully diluted basis, making it the largest US stock market debut so far in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: It implies a valuation on Cerebras on a fully diluted basis of $56.43 billion, making it the largest stock market debut so far this year.

key_facts.fact: The final price marks a sharp escalation from Cerebras's earlier marketing: it first disclosed a $115-$125 range on May 4 and a $23 billion valuation in a February funding round.
key_facts.excerpt: That's up from the $23 billion valuation Cerebras announced in February as part of a funding round.

key_facts.fact: Shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14 under ticker CBRS; underwriters hold a 30-day option for an additional 4.5 million shares.
key_facts.excerpt: The shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on May 14, 2026, under the ticker symbol 'CBRS.'

key_facts.fact: Co-founder and CEO Andrew Feldman holds a stake worth about $1.9 billion at the IPO price.
key_facts.excerpt: Andrew Feldman, Cerebras' co-founder and CEO, holds a stake worth about $1.9 billion.

stories.headline: RJ Scaringe's Mind Robotics Raises $400M Led by Kleiner Perkins

key_facts.fact: Mind Robotics announced a $400 million financing led by Kleiner Perkins on May 13, bringing total investment in the company to more than $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Mind Robotics today announced a $400 million financing led by Kleiner Perkins, bringing total investment in Mind Robotics to more than $1 billion.

key_facts.fact: The round included new investors Meritech Capital, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Incharge Capital, A-Star Capital and Garuda Ventures, plus existing backers Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Prysm Capital, Bain Capital Ventures and Greenoaks.
key_facts.excerpt: This financing included participation from new investors including Meritech Capital, Redpoint Ventures, SV Angel, Incharge Capital, A-Star Capital, and Garuda Ventures as well as existing investors including Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Prysm Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and Greenoaks.

key_facts.fact: The raise follows a $115M seed in late 2025 and a $500M Series A in March 2026; a source pegged the new valuation at $3.4 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: This follows a seed financing of $115M in late 2025 and a Series A of $500M in March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Mind Robotics, founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe in 2025 and based in Palo Alto, builds AI-powered industrial robots and uses Rivian's manufacturing lines as a live training environment.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded by RJ Scaringe in 2025, Mind Robotics is building the full-stack platform of foundation models, purpose-built robotics, and deployment infrastructure to automate industrial and manufacturing tasks at scale.

stories.headline: UK Inference Chip Startup Fractile Raises $220M Series B at ~$1B Valuation

key_facts.fact: UK-based AI inference chip startup Fractile closed a $220 million Series B round, announced May 13.
key_facts.excerpt: U.K.-based artificial intelligence inference chip startup Fractile Ltd. said today it has closed on a $220 million Series B round of funding.

key_facts.fact: The round was co-led by Accel, Factorial Funds and Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, with participation from Conviction, Gigascale, O1A, Felicis, Buckley Ventures and 8VC; it values Fractile at around $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Fractile, the UK AI inference chip startup, has raised $220 million at a valuation of around $1 billion. Investors were: Accel, Factorial Funds, Peter Thiel's Founders Fund, Conviction, Felicis, Buckley Ventures, 8VC and Gigascale Capital.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2022 by an Oxford PhD, Fractile builds chips and systems designed to overcome performance bottlenecks in large-scale AI inference; it had previously raised $17.5 million.
key_facts.excerpt: In July 2024, Fractile raised $15 million in seed funding... bringing its total funding to $17.5 million.

key_facts.fact: Fractile will use the funding to accelerate commercialization and deploy its first chips to customers, expanding hiring across offices in London, Bristol, San Francisco and Taipei.
key_facts.excerpt: Fractile said the new funding will help accelerate commercialization efforts and support deployment of its first chips and systems to customers. The company is also expanding hiring efforts across offices in London, Bristol, San Francisco, and Taipei.

stories.headline: US Has Cleared ~10 Chinese Firms to Buy Nvidia H200, But No Chips Have Shipped

key_facts.fact: The US has cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's H200 AI accelerator, but not a single chip has been delivered, according to three people briefed on the licences, first reported by Reuters on May 14.
key_facts.excerpt: The US has cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's H200, the company's second-most powerful AI accelerator, but not a single chip has been delivered, according to three people briefed on the licences and first reported by Reuters on 14 May.

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department licences cover Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com, alongside distributors including Lenovo and Foxconn, with each cleared customer permitted to buy up to 75,000 H200 units.
key_facts.excerpt: The approvals from the US Commerce Department cover Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com, alongside a handful of distributors, including Lenovo and Foxconn. Each cleared customer is permitted to buy up to 75,000 H200s under the licence terms.

key_facts.fact: Chinese buyers have held back after Beijing told domestic tech firms to pause H200 orders and pushed a parallel supply-chain security review to reduce dependence on US chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese buyers have held back after Beijing told domestic technology firms to pause H200 orders earlier this year, with the State Council pushing a parallel supply-chain security review aimed at reducing dependence on US chips.

key_facts.fact: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told a Senate hearing that the Chinese government has inhibited the purchases to protect its domestic chip industry; the Trump deal also requires 25% of chip-sale revenue to be paid to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick addressed the situation during a Senate hearing, noting that the Chinese government has inhibited these purchases to protect internal investments... The deal requires 25 percent of the revenue from chip sales to be paid to the US.

stories.headline: Foxconn Q1 Profit Rises 18.5% to $1.58B as AI Server Demand Surges

key_facts.fact: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision Industry) reported Q1 2026 net profit of T$49.92 billion ($1.58 billion), up 18.5% year-on-year and above Bloomberg estimates of T$48.43 billion, in results released May 14.
key_facts.excerpt: The world's largest contract electronics manufacturer posted a net profit of T$49.92 billion ($1.58 billion) in the three months to March 31, up 18.5% from last year. The print was higher than Bloomberg estimates of T$48.43 billion.

key_facts.fact: Q1 revenue jumped nearly 30% year-on-year to T$2.13 trillion (about $66.6 billion), a record, driven by AI server demand.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's Q1 revenue jumped nearly 30% to T$2.13 trillion.

key_facts.fact: For the first time, Foxconn's cloud and networking division, which assembles AI server racks, accounted for 41% of total revenue, surpassing the consumer electronics segment at 35%.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, Foxconn's cloud and networking division, which assembles AI server racks and related hardware, accounted for 41% of total revenue. Its consumer electronics segment, anchored by iPhone assembly for Apple Inc., came in at 35%.

key_facts.fact: Foxconn is a key supplier to Nvidia, assembling its most advanced AI servers, and expects operations to grow both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year in Q2 on AI-related products.
key_facts.excerpt: The Taiwanese company is a key supplier to Nvidia, and benefited greatly from rapidly increasing server demand in the artificial intelligence industry.

stories.headline: Cisco Posts Record $15.8B Q3 Revenue, Raises AI Orders Forecast, Cuts ~4,000 Jobs

key_facts.fact: Cisco reported Q3 FY26 record revenue of $15.84 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $1.06, both beating Wall Street estimates; net income rose to $3.37 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Earnings per share: $1.06 adjusted vs. $1.04 expected. Revenue: $15.84 billion vs. $15.56 billion expected. Revenue increased 12% in the quarter ended April 25... Net income rose to $3.37 billion.

key_facts.fact: AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers reached $1.9 billion in Q3, up from $600 million a year earlier; Cisco raised its full-year FY26 AI infrastructure order forecast to about $9 billion, up from $5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers reached $1.9 billion in Q3, up from $600 million last year... Full fiscal year 2026 AI infrastructure orders are expected to reach approximately $9 billion, which is 4.5 times FY25 levels.

key_facts.fact: Cisco said it will cut fewer than 4,000 jobs, less than 5% of its workforce, with most notifications beginning May 14; it expects pre-tax restructuring charges of up to $1 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: we are making changes today that will result in the reduction of our overall workforce in Q4 by fewer than 4,000 jobs, representing less than 5 percent of our total employee base. Most notifications will begin on May 14.

key_facts.fact: Cisco raised its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast to $62.8-$63 billion, up from $61.2-$61.7 billion; networking product orders grew more than 50% in Q3.
key_facts.excerpt: The company now expects fiscal 2026 revenue in the range of US$62.8-billion to US$63-billion, compared with its earlier forecast of US$61.2-billion to US$61.7-billion.

stories.headline: Blackstone Raises $1.75B in IPO of Data Center REIT BXDC

key_facts.fact: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust priced its IPO at $20 per share on May 13, selling 87.5 million shares to raise $1.75 billion; the REIT will trade on the NYSE under ticker BXDC starting May 14.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Inc. today announced the pricing of its initial public offering of 87.5 million shares of its common stock at a price to the public of $20.00 per share... expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on May 14, 2026 under the ticker symbol 'BXDC.'

key_facts.fact: The vehicle will target newly built data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion leased to investment-grade hyperscalers; it has not yet acquired any assets, making it a 'blind pool.'
key_facts.excerpt: The real estate investment trust will target newly built data centres valued at between US$250 million and US$1.5 billion and leased to investment-grade hyperscalers... the largest ever IPO of a Reit set up as a so-called blind pool.

key_facts.fact: BXDC plans to buy data centers in hubs including Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland and Austin, and targets returns of 5.75% to 7% or higher.
key_facts.excerpt: BXDC plans to buy newly built data centers in hubs like Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin, focusing on big properties already leased to 'hyperscalers.'

key_facts.fact: If the underwriters' 30-day option is exercised in full, gross proceeds would reach $2.0 billion; the offering is led by Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, among others.
key_facts.excerpt: If the option to purchase additional shares is exercised in full, the gross proceeds of the offering will be $2.0 billion.
